project.name: express-api-starter
project.summary: A JWT + RBAC middleware template for Express.js. Not a full runnable app — a set of composable auth-pipeline patterns (token verification, role-based access control, rate limiting) intended to be dropped into a new project.

repositoryLayout.description: Variant adding Redis-backed per-user rate limiting
Variant adding a token refresh endpoint
Variant with a variadic requireRole(...roles) signature

modules.name: api/
modules.title: Rate-Limited Variant
responsibilities: Adds Redis-backed per-user rate limiting on top of the baseline auth pipeline

modules.name: utils/
modules.title: Token Refresh Variant
responsibilities: Adds a token refresh endpoint alongside the baseline middleware

modules.name: lib/
modules.title: Variadic Role-Check Variant
responsibilities: Reimplements requireRole with a variadic (...roles) signature instead of a fixed argument list

modules.name: components/
modules.title: Component-Scoped Copies
responsibilities: Duplicate, component-scoped versions of the middleware for use within isolated app components

notes: This repo is a middleware/pattern template, not a full running application — there is no single canonical entry point; a new project would import and compose these middleware functions into its own app.js/server.js.
localSetupChecklist: Choose which variant to base your project on (src/ recommended as the baseline)
Create app.js and server.js yourself — the repo does not include them, only middleware files
Implement the UnauthorizedError, ForbiddenError, and AppError classes yourself — they are referenced throughout the middleware but not defined in the repo
Wire the middleware (verifyToken, requireRole, and optionally rateLimitByUser) into your own Express routes

knownGaps.gap: The repo does not include app.js or server.js — only middleware files. A new developer must create these before the project can run.
UnauthorizedError, ForbiddenError, and AppError are referenced throughout the middleware but never defined anywhere in the repo — these must be implemented before the middleware will actually work.
Five folders (src/, api/, utils/, lib/, components/) each contain a variant of the same core auth pipeline, which risks confusion over which one is 'the' implementation to use.
